sources.says: $0.20 per listing; 6.5% transaction fee on the price you display (US sellers: not on sales tax); Offsite Ads 15%, or 12% for shops over $10,000 in the past 365 days.
Titles can be up to 140 characters.
Up to 13 tags per listing; each tag up to 20 characters.
Up to five files per digital listing, 20MB each.
Shop settings have a post-purchase Message to Buyers, with a separate message for digital items.

Sales on Gumroad's website: 10% + $0.50 per transaction, plus sales tax; this does not include credit card processing (2.9% + $0.30) or PayPal fees. Discover marketplace sales: a flat 30% that includes all processing fees.
Products can be free or up to USD 5,000; a + after the minimum price (like $5+) lets buyers pay what they want; product types include a bundle of existing products.

Upsells tab on the Checkout page: suggest another product, replace the cart with another product (for example a bundle that contains it), or offer an upgraded version; shown after the buyer presses Pay.
The Emails dashboard sends to subscribers and customers once you have earned $100 after fees and received a payout.
Image Pins: title 100 characters max, description up to 800 characters; BMP, JPEG, PNG, TIFF or WEBP up to 20 MB.
Recommended 2:3 aspect ratio, or 1000 x 1500 pixels; the first 40 characters of a title may show in feeds.

reviews.rule: Nothing in exchange for a review: no free item, discount, refund, entry or cash, and no asking only happy buyers.

sources.says: Etsy's Anti-Shilling policy: compensating someone with free or reduced items, samples or cash for a biased positive review is shilling.
16 CFR 465.4: a business may not provide compensation or other incentives in exchange for reviews that express a particular sentiment, positive or negative.
